population.note: Figures are approximate estimates pending Census reconciliation, consistent with the caveat practice established in the Oklahoma City and Dallas JSON files.

recommendations.name: Weller Book Works
recommendations.note: Running since 1929 (as Zion's Bookstore, then Sam Weller's); Sam Weller stocked contraband Henry Miller and D.H. Lawrence for customers who asked, and the store now runs a standing 'Banned! from Utah Schools' display case -- literary-freedom politics built into the shelving.

recommendations.name: The King's English Bookshop
recommendations.note: SLC's other long-running community-anchor indie -- packed events calendar, staff-pick culture, and the kind of shop the Guardian has written up for how it operates differently from a standard indie.

recommendations.name: Ken Sanders Rare Books
recommendations.note: Ken Sanders co-owned the 1970s countercultural shop The Cosmic Aeroplane before opening this ABAA rare-book operation in 1997 -- deep stock in Western Americana, rare and esoteric volumes, and counterculture ephemera; a Salt Lake institution for collectors of the strange and the political alike.

recommendations.name: The Legendarium
recommendations.note: Genre specialist focused on sci-fi, fantasy, and horror, with an on-site cafe -- the direct hit for the horror-and-occult reading interest.

recommendations.name: Boing! Anarchist Collective
recommendations.bestTimeOfDay: Evening for a reading or discussion
recommendations.note: Mandatory radical/infoshop search result: a nine-plus-year anarchist community space hosting radical dialog, readings, and performances -- not a retail bookstore, but the closest thing SLC has to an infoshop, and explicitly welcomes LGBTQ+, anticapitalist, and countercultural community.

recommendations.name: The Heavy Metal Shop
recommendations.note: Iconic metal-and-punk vinyl, patches, and merch shop operating since 1987 -- the well-known/must-see anchor of SLC's heavy-music retail scene.

recommendations.name: Diabolical Records
recommendations.note: Psych, punk, garage, electronic, and local pressings, plus a real DIY-scene tie: hosts Bandemonium (musicians randomly re-shuffled into new bands) and touring acts like Soft Kill and Cool Ghouls.

recommendations.name: Raunch Records & Skate
recommendations.note: 'Raw, loud, and unapologetically punk' since the 1980s -- a hard-to-find-underground-music specialist that doubles as a skate shop and gathering point for the city's punk/hardcore community.

recommendations.name: Randy's Record Shop
recommendations.note: Deep breadth-and-depth general vinyl, CD, and tape stock spanning new releases and classics -- a longstanding SLC institution.

recommendations.name: Memento Mori
recommendations.note: Part barbershop, part art gallery, part record cave -- an eclectic hybrid shop whose name alone is a direct hit for the horror/occult interest.

recommendations.name: Salt Lake Roasting Co.
recommendations.note: Established 1981, the pioneer of specialty coffee in a state where coffee is culturally uncommon -- Visit Utah compares its local role to Starbucks in Seattle. The single strongest 'unique because of the surrounding culture' pick in this list.

recommendations.name: Publik Coffee Roasters
recommendations.note: Major local roaster operating out of a renovated warehouse, emphasizing responsibly sourced beans across several SLC locations.

recommendations.name: La Barba
recommendations.note: Third-wave espresso and pour-over pairing with fresh pastries in an atmospheric downtown space.

recommendations.name: Alchemy Coffee
recommendations.note: Neighborhood specialty spot with a community-oriented, no-frills vibe -- a regular on locals' shortlists.

recommendations.name: Coffee Garden
recommendations.note: Long-running indie community hangout in the 9th & 9th district, the kind of shop with regulars who've been coming for decades.

recommendations.name: Les Madeleines
recommendations.bestTimeOfDay: Morning, before the case sells out
recommendations.note: James Beard-recognized baker famous for kouign-amann ('kouing aman') -- the well-known/must-eat pastry stop in the city, and it also ships nationwide via Goldbelly if you can't make it in person.

recommendations.name: Mrs. Backer's Pastry Shop
recommendations.note: A decades-old Sugar House institution -- handcrafted cakes, cookies, and eclairs, the kind of place locals order birthday cakes from generation after generation.

recommendations.name: Tulie Bakery
recommendations.note: Modern, minimalist bakery known for almond, bacon-and-egg, and ham-and-cheese croissants plus lemon tarts and morning buns.

recommendations.name: Fillings & Emulsions
recommendations.note: Cuban-inspired pastry program (guava, passion fruit, Opera cake) that's also notably gluten-free friendly -- the most distinctive technique angle in this category.

recommendations.name: Eva's Bakery
recommendations.note: French-leaning downtown bakery known for strawberry croissants in a photogenic blue-and-white space.

recommendations.name: Fry Sauce
recommendations.note: The ketchup-and-mayo condiment invented in Salt Lake City in the 1950s -- the single most SLC-coded thing to order, best tried at Hires Big H, a since-1959 drive-in institution.

recommendations.name: Pastrami Burger
recommendations.note: A beef patty topped with pastrami, cheese, and fry sauce on a sesame bun -- popularized at Crown Burgers.

recommendations.name: Funeral Potatoes
recommendations.note: A cheesy potato casserole with a cornflake topping, traditionally served at LDS funeral luncheons and now a year-round comfort dish across Utah restaurants.

recommendations.name: Barely Buzzed Cheese
recommendations.note: An award-winning espresso-and-lavender-rubbed cheddar from Beehive Cheese Co. -- one of TasteAtlas's top-rated Utah cheeses, and a direct hit for both the coffee and bee interests via the maker's own name.

recommendations.name: Frog Eye Salad
recommendations.note: A whimsically named pasta salad (acini di pepe, egg yolks, whipped cream, optional pineapple/marshmallow) that TasteAtlas rates among the region's most divisive dishes -- worth trying purely for the novelty.

recommendations.name: Caputo's Market Gift Boxes
recommendations.note: SLC's essential gourmet deli/market ships curated boxes of cheeses, oils, vinegars, and specialty meats -- the well-known/must-see one-stop for mailable local flavor.

recommendations.name: Local Honey — BEEZ Hives N Honey
recommendations.note: Beekeeper-owned shop selling truly local raw honey from backyard and small-batch Wasatch Front apiaries, plus propolis, pollen, beeswax, and miniature gift-favor jars -- the most literal bee-interest pick in the whole guide.

recommendations.name: Barely Buzzed Cheese (to mail)
recommendations.note: Same espresso-lavender cheddar as the dish pick above -- shelf-stable enough (vacuum-sealed) to travel well as a mailed gift; Caputo's ships it.

recommendations.name: Z's Salsa & Hot Sauce
recommendations.note: Small-batch four-pepper salsa and a spicy Bloody Mary mix, handcrafted locally and sold through farmers markets and Etsy -- easy to mail.

recommendations.name: Ritual Chocolate
recommendations.note: Small-batch bean-to-bar craft chocolate from just outside the metro, with rotating single-origin bars including an El Salvadoran-espresso pairing -- ships and mails well.

recommendations.name: Gilgal Sculpture Garden
recommendations.note: A free outsider-art garden built mid-20th-century by Thomas Battersby Child Jr. -- 12 sculptures and 70+ inscribed stones blending Mormon scripture, poetry, and literary texts, tucked behind a Chuck-a-Rama parking lot.

recommendations.name: Summum Pyramid
recommendations.note: A religious sect founded in 1975 blending science-fiction cosmology and Egyptian polytheism, practicing modern mummification, with public tours by appointment on Wednesday evenings -- as strange and occult-adjacent a stop as this guide gets.

recommendations.name: Lilly E. Gray's Grave — "Victim of the Beast 666"

citedFrom.label: Atlas Obscura -- Victim of the Beast 666 Gravestone

recommendations.note: A tombstone inscribed 'Victim of the Beast 666' in the largest municipally owned cemetery in the U.S. -- Lilly died of natural causes, but her husband believed government conspiracy killed her.

recommendations.name: This Is the Place Heritage Park
recommendations.note: The well-known/must-see anchor of SLC pioneer history -- marks where Brigham Young reportedly declared 'this is the right place' in 1847, with a living-history pioneer village on the grounds.

recommendations.name: Antelope Island State Park
recommendations.bestTimeOfDay: Morning for bison activity; sunset for lake views
recommendations.note: The natural-attraction balance pick: a free-roaming bison and pronghorn herd on an island in the Great Salt Lake, plus hiking, cycling, and internationally certified dark-sky stargazing, about 40 minutes from downtown.

recommendations.name: Sugar House Park — Joe Hill Execution Site & 2023 Monument
recommendations.note: A public park built on the site of the former Sugar House Prison, where Wobbly songwriter Joe Hill was executed by firing squad in 1915 after a controversial trial. In 2023 the Central Utah Federation of Labor (AFL-CIO) unveiled a monument near the execution site -- this guide's analyticalThread anchor.

recommendations.name: Kilby Court
recommendations.note: SLC's longest-running all-ages venue, open since 1999 -- a converted garage that's launched Death Cab for Cutie, Phoebe Bridgers, Mitski, and Japanese Breakfast on the way up.

recommendations.name: The Urban Lounge
recommendations.note: Long-running indie/punk-leaning bar venue, a core stop on SLC's local and touring circuit.

recommendations.name: The Depot
recommendations.note: A larger historic concert hall near the old Rio Grande railroad depot, booking rock, metal, and hardcore-adjacent touring acts alongside bigger indie names.

recommendations.name: Boing! Anarchist Collective (as a show space)
recommendations.note: Same space as the bookstores-category pick — its 'performances' programming crosses into DIY show territory, making it SLC's clearest example of a venue doubling as explicit political community space.

recommendations.name: Diabolical Records In-Stores / Bandemonium
recommendations.note: Same shop as the records-category pick — its in-store sets and Bandemonium nights are the city's most direct record-store-as-venue tie.

recommendations.name: Visit Salt Lake Store (Ashley Collett Design)
recommendations.note: The official downtown visitor-center shop carries stickers, magnets, and pins designed by local Utah artist Ashley Collett -- a locally-designed alternative to generic tourist-shop magnets.

recommendations.name: Salt & Honey Market
recommendations.note: A curated Utah-themed gift shop (name notwithstanding) featuring local vendors and artists — postcards, prints, honey, and topographic-patch apparel emphasizing locally-designed goods over mass-produced tourist product.

recommendations.name: Memento Mori (prints & oddities)
recommendations.note: Same barbershop/gallery/record-cave hybrid as the records pick — its gallery side sells local art and prints with more edge than a standard magnet rack.

recommendations.name: Weller Book Works — "Banned!" Merch & Postcards
recommendations.note: Same shop as the bookstores pick — postcards and totes tied to its 'Banned! from Utah Schools' display make for a souvenir with a literal political statement attached.

recommendations.name: BEEZ Hives N Honey (gift jars & beeswax candles)
recommendations.note: Same shop as the mailable-gifts pick — miniature honey jars and beeswax candles double as the most literal bee-themed souvenir in the city.

recommendations.name: Make Salt Lake
recommendations.note: The city's flagship community makerspace -- 3D printing, laser cutting, woodworking, and electronics under one roof, with regular open houses and Meetup-listed events.

recommendations.name: 801 Labs
recommendations.note: A hackerspace with a strong cybersecurity/electronics-hacking bent -- meetups, workshops, and open lab nights for hardware and software tinkerers alike.

recommendations.name: Squarewave Sound
recommendations.bestTimeOfDay: Wed–Fri 12–6pm, Sat 12–5pm (per shop's own site — see status note)
recommendations.note: Self-described 'SLC's only synth shop' -- Eurorack modular, drum machines, and effects pedals, authorized dealer for Moog/Korg/Novation, with occasional community meetups and classes.

recommendations.name: Craft Lake City DIY Festival
recommendations.note: SLC's annual flagship maker event -- 500+ local makers, food vendors, and performers; not a fixed space, but the clearest single snapshot of the city's DIY/maker culture in one place.

filmedHere.title: SLC Punk!
filmedHere.visitNote: Public high school still operating; exterior/hallway shots used for the fictional school. Confrontation scene shot on the historic quad. Heroin Bob's funeral sequence filmed here; still an active Catholic cathedral, open to visitors. Used for the film's LSD sequence. Site of Stevo's punk-rock monologue; the mall was demolished and redeveloped, so this location can no longer be visited as filmed.

filmedHere.title: High School Musical
filmedHere.visitNote: All three films used East High's real hallways, cafeteria, and gym (Troy's 'Wildcats' are fictional -- East High's real team is the Leopards). A functioning public school; call ahead to arrange a tour.

filmedHere.title: The Sandlot
filmedHere.visitNote: The dirt lot behind several private homes on Glenrose Drive; still privately owned by the residents, so it's viewable from the street only, not enterable.

filmedHere.title: Dumb and Dumber
filmedHere.visitNote: Interiors shot at Intermountain Studios in Orem (built by the Osmonds); the frozen mini-bike arrival scene was shot on Main Street in Park City, not Aspen, CO, where the film is set.

bornHere.name: Bill Haywood
bornHere.note: Founding member and General Secretary-Treasurer of the Industrial Workers of the World (IWW); his formative organizing happened in Idaho/Western mining, but he was born in SLC. See analyticalThread.

bornHere.name: Neal Cassady
bornHere.note: Beat Generation figure who inspired the character Dean Moriarty in Jack Kerouac's On the Road; born in SLC, though most of his life was lived in Denver and San Francisco.

bornHere.name: Natacha Rambova
bornHere.note: Silent-film costume/art director (and wife of Rudolph Valentino) who later became a serious Egyptologist and occult writer -- a genuine film-meets-esoterica crossover.

bornHere.name: Roseanne Barr
bornHere.note: Comedian and creator/star of Roseanne -- included as the well-known/must-mention balance pick for this list.
